sentences.text: Kepodactylus possessed a wingspan of about 2.5 meters and featured additional pneumatic foramina in its vertebrae and humerus.
Gregory S. Paul estimated the mass of this creature at approximately 10 kilograms, or 22 lbs, in 2022.
The species name insperatus means "unhoped-for" because the researchers originally hoped to find a dinosaur, not a pterosaur.
The genus name Kepodactylus combines Greek words for "garden" and "finger" to reference its discovery site and pterosaur anatomy.
Fossils of Kepodactylus were discovered in 1992 in Garden Park, Colorado, while a team excavated a Stegosaurus specimen.
Jerald Harris and Kenneth Carpenter named the genus Kepodactylus and its type species K. insperatus in 1996.
The holotype specimen DMNH 21684 consists of a cervical vertebra, a left humerus, finger bones, and a metatarsal.
David Unwin considered Kepodactylus to be a basal member of the Dsungaripteroidea.
Kepodactylus lived during the Late Jurassic period in the Morrison Formation of Colorado, United States.
